fix.notes: The regex `\b(?:[a-zA-Z]-)+[a-zA-Z]\b` only matches tokens where every hyphen-separated segment is exactly one letter, so common hyphenated names like Blue-Red or 12-Rack are unaffected. No existing test cases were broken by the change.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

Deck names composed of single letters separated by hyphens (e.g. `o-o-p-s a-l-l`) produced inconsistent casing after sanitization. The `titlecase` library capitalizes the first letter of words starting with "a" only when it's the first word — so `o-o-p-s` became `O-O-P-S` (correct) but `a-l-l` became `a-L-L` (the leading `a` was left lowercase because `titlecase` treats it as a small word, yet the letters after each hyphen were still capitalized). The result `O-O-P-S a-L-L` looks bizarre.

## What changed

Added `normalize_single_letter_hyphenated()` in `decksite/deck_name.py`, called immediately after the final `titlecase.titlecase()` in `normalize()`. It uses `re.sub` to find any token where every hyphen-delimited segment is exactly one letter (`\b(?:[a-zA-Z]-)+[a-zA-Z]\b`) and converts it to uppercase. This turns `a-L-L` → `A-L-L` and leaves already-correct tokens like `O-O-P-S` unchanged.

Added a corresponding test case to `TESTDATA` in `deck_name_test.py`.

## How it was validated

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (all checks)
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit decksite/deck_name_test.py` — 846 passed, 1 skipped (the skip is a pre-existing unrelated functional test)
- Manually verified the regex does not incorrectly match multi-letter hyphenated tokens (`Blue-Red`, `Elves-N-Taxes3`, `12-Rack`, `Mono-W`, etc.) by tracing word-boundary logic.

Fixes #11320
